name: Health Innovation Hub (H2i)
organization: Temerty Faculty of Medicine, University of Toronto
eligibility_summary: Campus-linked accelerator for U of T-affiliated health innovators — clinicians, researchers, students, and faculty in the Temerty Faculty of Medicine ecosystem and partner hospitals.
description: H2i is the Health Innovation Hub of the Temerty Faculty of Medicine. It supports early-stage health ventures founded by U of T-affiliated clinicians, researchers, and students. H2i offers mentorship, structured programming, and connections to clinical validation partners across UHN, SickKids, Unity Health, and other partner institutions. As of its 2024-25 reporting, ~60% of supported ventures have female co-founders and ~28% have Black co-founders. H2i also runs a long-term partnership with the Mastercard Foundation supporting ventures across Africa.
what_makes_it_distinctive: Direct access to clinician mentors and hospital partners for validation. Strong equity focus. Connects ventures to the Lab2Market national program.
source_note: Verified against H2i annual report 2024-25 and h2i.utoronto.ca

name: MaRS Discovery District
eligibility_summary: Open to high-growth Canadian ventures across health, cleantech, enterprise, and fintech. Health vertical is the largest cluster.
description: MaRS is one of North America's largest innovation hubs, with a dedicated health vertical that has supported thousands of health-tech ventures since 2005. Programming includes advisory services, talent connections, customer development support, and capital introductions. MaRS is physically located adjacent to U of T and the hospital district, which makes co-location and partnership with clinical sites practical.
what_makes_it_distinctive: Scale and breadth — most established health-tech ecosystem hub in Canada. Strong corporate and government partnerships.

name: JLABS @ Toronto
eligibility_summary: Life-sciences companies developing pharmaceutical, medical device, consumer health, or digital health solutions. Companies retain full ownership of IP — JLABS takes no equity.
description: JLABS @ Toronto is part of Johnson & Johnson Innovation's global JLABS network of life-sciences incubators. Provides wet lab and office space, access to specialized equipment, and a curated mentorship and partnership network. Companies retain 100% of equity and IP — JLABS does not invest directly, but JJDC (J&J's venture arm) sometimes does as a separate transaction. Hosts Quickfire Challenge grant competitions.
what_makes_it_distinctive: Wet-lab infrastructure access without giving up equity — rare for hardware/wet-lab biotech in Canada. Direct line to J&J therapeutic-area leaders.

name: Creative Destruction Lab (CDL-Toronto)
organization: Rotman School of Management, University of Toronto
eligibility_summary: Seed-stage, science-based ventures. Health stream takes both therapeutics and digital health. Highly selective.
description: CDL is an objectives-based program for seed-stage science and technology ventures. Founders are matched with a cohort of mentors ('Fellows') — typically successful founders and operators — who set quarterly objectives. Ventures that fail to hit objectives are dropped between sessions. CDL-Toronto runs a dedicated Health stream covering therapeutics, devices, and digital health.
what_makes_it_distinctive: Quarterly objective-setting with elite Fellow group; selective drop-out structure forces focus.

name: Ontario Bioscience Innovation Organization (OBIO)
eligibility_summary: Ontario-based health-science companies. Programs include CAAP (Capital Access Advisory Program), H2BB (Health to Business Bridge), and talent programs.
description: OBIO is a not-for-profit, member-based organization advancing the commercialization of human health technologies in Ontario. Runs CAAP (Capital Access Advisory Program) for Series A-ready companies, the Health to Business Bridge for early-stage founders, and several talent-funding programs supporting hiring at Ontario health-science companies.
what_makes_it_distinctive: Specifically Ontario-focused; strong programs on the capital-readiness and talent sides. Acts as the de facto industry association.

name: Centre for Commercialization of Regenerative Medicine (CCRM)
eligibility_summary: Companies and academic groups working in cell therapy, gene therapy, and regenerative medicine.
description: CCRM is a public-private consortium for commercializing regenerative medicine and cell and gene therapies. It provides process development, manufacturing, and venture creation services. Co-founded multiple regenerative-medicine companies and is connected to OmniaBio, a contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO).
what_makes_it_distinctive: Specialized infrastructure for cell and gene therapy — process development and manufacturing access that founders cannot get elsewhere in Canada.

name: NRC IRAP (Industrial Research Assistance Program)
eligibility_summary: Canadian incorporated for-profit SMEs (<500 employees) with R&D-driven projects. Engagement starts with an Industrial Technology Advisor (ITA).
description: IRAP is Canada's flagship non-dilutive funding program for SMEs doing technology R&D. Funding amounts range from small advisory engagements to multi-hundred-thousand-dollar project grants. Engagement is gated through assignment to an ITA, who scopes a fundable project. Process can take several months from first contact to first dollar.
what_makes_it_distinctive: Non-dilutive, available across stages, and well-recognized by downstream investors as a validation signal. The ITA relationship matters more than the application form.

name: Mitacs Accelerate
eligibility_summary: Canadian companies that want to collaborate with a Canadian university researcher. Mitacs matches company contribution 1:1 (or better) to fund a graduate-student or postdoc intern on a defined research project.
description: Mitacs Accelerate matches a company's contribution to fund a graduate-student or postdoc intern working on a defined R&D project in collaboration with a Canadian academic supervisor. The minimum unit is a 4-month internship; funding tiers go up substantially for longer engagements. Frequently used by health-tech startups to access U of T / Waterloo / McGill research capacity at subsidized rates.
what_makes_it_distinctive: Lowers the cost of accessing academic R&D talent. Excellent fit for startups that need a specific technical investigation done but can't afford a full hire.

name: Lab2Market (L2M)
organization: National network — anchored at multiple Canadian universities
eligibility_summary: Graduate students and postdocs exploring commercialization of their research. Cohort-based with multiple themed streams (health, cleantech, ocean, etc.).
description: Lab2Market is a national customer-discovery training program for graduate students and postdocs considering commercializing their research. Built on the NSF I-Corps model. Cohort-based. Stipend funded, with structured customer-discovery curriculum and mentorship. The Health stream is run in partnership with H2i and other health-innovation partners.
what_makes_it_distinctive: Customer-discovery training specifically designed for academic researchers who have technology but no business background. The Health stream is one of the most direct entry points into commercialization for U of T health researchers.
source_note: Verified against lab2market.ca and H2i 2024-25 annual report

name: DMZ
eligibility_summary: Tech-enabled startups. Multiple cohort tiers (Incubator, Accelerator, Scale).
description: DMZ is the startup accelerator at Toronto Metropolitan University. Sector-agnostic but has an active health-tech cluster. Provides mentorship, customer and investor introductions, and access to a peer founder community. Multiple program tiers depending on stage.
what_makes_it_distinctive: Strong founder community and brand recognition for Canadian tech. Best fit for digital health / software-heavy ventures rather than wet-lab or device companies.

name: Velocity
eligibility_summary: Open to founders associated with the University of Waterloo (students, alumni, faculty). Strong representation across software, hardware, and health-tech.
description: Velocity is the University of Waterloo's startup incubator. Programming spans idea-stage through seed. Runs the Velocity Fund pitch competition with substantial cash prizes for top teams. Has produced multiple health-tech and biotech ventures, with growing emphasis on the Waterloo health-research ecosystem.
what_makes_it_distinctive: Equity-free support model. Strong technical-founder culture. Geographically distinct from Toronto but well-connected to the Toronto ecosystem.

name: FedDev Ontario
eligibility_summary: For-profit businesses, not-for-profits, and ecosystem organizations in Southern Ontario. Programs have specific intake windows.
description: Federal Economic Development Agency for Southern Ontario. Administers several programs that fund business scale-up, innovation ecosystem support, and regional economic development. Application processes are formal and intake windows are program-specific. Often used by scaling health-tech companies to fund capacity expansion.
what_makes_it_distinctive: Government-scale funding (six- to seven-figure contributions) for established companies ready to scale. Slow process but large amounts.
